senses.gloss: A piece of furniture with open shelves on top and a closed cabinet below.
examples: Her grandmother's china is displayed in the *hutch*.
We're refinishing an old oak *hutch* for the dining room.
The desk came with a *hutch* for books and files.

senses.gloss: A car that runs on both a gasoline engine and an electric motor.
examples: They traded the pickup for a *hybrid* to save on gas.
*Hybrids* get much better mileage in city traffic.
The dealership had one *hybrid* left on the lot.

senses.gloss: Something that combines two different types or styles.
examples: The show is a *hybrid* of talk show and game show.
Their schedule is a *hybrid*: three days in the office, two at home.
This bike is a *hybrid*, part road bike and part mountain bike.

senses.gloss: The force of one object striking another, or the moment of the strike.
examples: The bumper crumpled on *impact*.
The *impact* of the collision threw both cars into the median.
Helmets are built to spread the force of an *impact*.

senses.gloss: The business or act of bringing goods into a country from abroad.
examples: The *import* of foreign steel fell sharply last year.
Congress voted to restrict the *import* of certain pesticides.
Her job is managing the *import* of coffee from Brazil.

senses.gloss: A mark left on a surface by pressing something into it.
examples: Her boots left deep *imprints* in the wet sand.
The tire left a clear *imprint* in the mud.
You could still see the *imprint* of the coin in the clay.

senses.gloss: A lasting effect that a person or event leaves on something.
examples: Her teaching left an *imprint* on a whole generation of students.
The war left its *imprint* on every family in town.
You can see the architect's *imprint* all over the building.

senses.gloss: A short electrical or nerve signal traveling along a wire or a nerve.
examples: Nerve *impulses* travel from the eye to the brain.
The sensor sends an electrical *impulse* to the control box.
Damaged nerves carry *impulses* more slowly.

senses.gloss: A tray on a desk where incoming papers are left.
examples: Leave the signed forms in my *inbox*.
Her *inbox* was buried under a stack of files.
The mail clerk drops the day's letters into each *inbox*.

senses.gloss: A dark blue dye, originally made from a plant, used especially on denim.
examples: The jeans are dyed with natural *indigo*.
Farmers here once grew *indigo* for export.
*Indigo* fades a little with every wash.

senses.gloss: An unwillingness to act or change that keeps things as they are.
examples: Nothing changed, mostly out of plain *inertia*.
The bill died of bureaucratic *inertia*.
It took a crisis to overcome the company's *inertia*.

senses.gloss: The earliest stage in the development of something.
examples: Electric aircraft are still in their *infancy*.
The technology was in its *infancy* when they invested.
Online shopping was in its *infancy* back then.

senses.gloss: The dark liquid a squid or octopus squirts out to hide itself.
examples: The squid shot out a cloud of *ink* and vanished.
The pasta is colored black with squid *ink*.
An octopus releases *ink* when a predator comes close.

senses.gloss: Tattoos on a person's skin (informal).
examples: He's got a lot of *ink* on his forearms.
She got her first *ink* at eighteen.
Most of his *ink* stays hidden under his sleeves.

senses.gloss: An opening through which liquid or air enters a machine.
examples: Check that the water *inlet* isn't clogged.
Cold air is drawn in through the *inlet* on the side.
The pump has an *inlet* at the bottom and an outlet on top.

senses.gloss: Advice, ideas, or comments that someone contributes.
examples: I'd like your *input* before I send the proposal.
The team had no *input* into the final decision.
Thanks for all your *input* at the meeting.

senses.gloss: A piece made to fit inside something else.
examples: She wears gel *inserts* in her running shoes.
The mold has a steel *insert* that shapes the hole.
The crib mattress came with a waterproof *insert*.

senses.gloss: An opening or pipe through which air, water, or fuel enters an engine or system.
examples: Leaves had blocked the water *intake*.
He installed a cold-air *intake* on the truck.
Snow packed into the *intake* and stalled the engine.

senses.gloss: A tall garden plant with large showy flowers and flat, sword-shaped leaves.
examples: The *irises* along the fence bloom in late May.
She cut an armful of purple *irises* for the table.
A clump of wild *iris* grew at the edge of the pond.

senses.gloss: Clothes that are waiting to be ironed or have just been ironed.
examples: There's a whole basket of *ironing* in the laundry room.
She put the *ironing* away before dinner.
A pile of *ironing* sat on the end of the bed.

senses.gloss: A raised area in the middle of a road that divides the lanes or shelters people crossing.
examples: Wait on the *island* until the light changes.
The truck jumped the curb and hit the concrete *island*.
A row of shrubs runs down the *island* between the lanes.

senses.gloss: A freestanding counter unit standing in the middle of a kitchen.
examples: The kids do their homework at the kitchen *island*.
We put the sink in the *island*.
There are four stools along one side of the *island*.

senses.gloss: An important subject that people discuss or disagree about.
examples: Health care was the biggest *issue* in the election.
The mayor refused to take a position on the *issue*.
They disagree on almost every *issue*.

senses.gloss: A problem or fault with something.
examples: We're having *issues* with the printer again.
If there's any *issue* with your order, call us.
The car has an *issue* with the transmission.

senses.gloss: A restless desire to do something.
examples: He had an *itch* to get back on the road.
She felt the old *itch* to start painting again.
After two years in one town, the *itch* came back.

senses.gloss: A short piece of news in a paper or a broadcast.
examples: There was a small *item* about the fire on page six.
The station ran a two-minute *item* on the flood.
She reads the business *items* first.

senses.gloss: Two people who are dating each other (informal).
examples: Everyone at work knows they're an *item*.
The two of them became an *item* over the summer.
Are those two an *item* now?

senses.gloss: A creamy white color, a little warmer than pure white.
examples: We painted the trim a soft *ivory*.
She chose *ivory* instead of white for the dress.
The walls are done in *ivory* with white molding.

senses.gloss: The playing card ranking between the ten and the queen.
examples: She drew the *jack* of hearts.
A pair of *jacks* was enough to win the hand.
He needed a *jack* to finish the straight.

senses.gloss: A socket that a plug fits into for sound, phone, or network cables.
examples: The new phone has no headphone *jack*.
Plug the microphone into the *jack* on the front panel.
Every room has a phone *jack* by the door.

senses.gloss: A paper or cardboard cover that goes around a book or a record.
examples: The dust *jacket* was torn, but the book was fine.
His photo is on the back of the *jacket*.
The album *jackets* were stacked against the wall.

senses.gloss: A mass of people, vehicles, or things packed so tightly that nothing can move.
examples: We sat in a *jam* on the interstate for an hour.
The copier has a paper *jam* again.
There was a *jam* at the exit doors after the concert.

senses.gloss: A difficult situation that is hard to get out of (informal).
examples: He called from the police station; he was in a real *jam*.
She got into a *jam* with her landlord over the rent.
Thanks for getting me out of a *jam*.

senses.gloss: An informal session where musicians play together without planning it.
examples: There's an open *jam* at the bar on Thursdays.
The band's best songs came out of late-night *jams*.
A few friends came over for a *jam* in the garage.

senses.gloss: One of the two parts of a tool or machine that grip or crush something.
examples: Tighten the *jaws* of the vise around the pipe.
The wrench's *jaws* were worn smooth.
The clamp has rubber *jaws* so it won't scratch the wood.

senses.gloss: A soft, semi-solid substance that shakes when it is moved.
examples: Petroleum *jelly* keeps chapped lips from cracking.
His legs turned to *jelly* at the top of the ladder.
The broth cooled overnight into a firm *jelly*.

senses.gloss: A soft, stretchy knitted cloth used for T-shirts and casual clothes.
examples: The sheets are cotton *jersey*, soft as an old T-shirt.
She wore a gray *jersey* dress to the office.
*Jersey* stretches, so it hardly wrinkles.

senses.gloss: A narrow stream of liquid or gas forced out under pressure.
examples: A *jet* of steam shot out of the valve.
*Jets* of water rose from the fountain.
He aimed a *jet* of water at the muddy tires.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that is greatly valued.
examples: That little bakery is the *jewel* of the neighborhood.
The old library is the *jewel* of the campus.
Our babysitter is a *jewel*.

senses.gloss: A fast, lively folk dance, or the music played for it.
examples: The fiddler struck up a *jig*.
He danced a little *jig* when he heard the news.
The band played reels and *jigs* all night.

senses.gloss: A device that holds a piece of work and guides the tool cutting it.
examples: He built a *jig* to drill the holes in exactly the same spot.
A simple *jig* keeps every cut square.
The shop uses a *jig* for each dovetail joint.

senses.gloss: A light ringing sound made by small metal objects knocking together.
examples: I heard the *jingle* of keys in the hallway.
The dog came running at the *jingle* of his leash.
There was a faint *jingle* of coins in his pocket.

senses.gloss: A particular piece of work that has to be done.
examples: Painting the fence is a two-day *job*.
I have a few *jobs* to finish around the house this weekend.
Cleaning the gutters is the worst *job* of the fall.

senses.gloss: A crime, especially a robbery (informal).
examples: The police think it was an inside *job*.
They pulled a bank *job* in broad daylight.
He served ten years for a *job* he swore he didn't do.

senses.gloss: A place where two parts of a structure are joined together.
examples: Water was leaking from a *joint* in the pipe.
The *joints* in the sidewalk are filled with tar.
Every *joint* in the frame is glued and screwed.

senses.gloss: A small, cheap restaurant, bar, or club (informal).
examples: There's a burger *joint* two blocks from here.
It's a decent enough *joint* for a weeknight.
We ate at a pizza *joint* near the stadium.

senses.gloss: A hand-rolled marijuana cigarette (informal).
examples: They passed a *joint* around the campfire.
He was ticketed for a *joint* in his pocket.
Someone lit a *joint* in the parking lot.

senses.gloss: Something or someone too poor or ridiculous to be taken seriously.
examples: The whole investigation was a *joke*.
Their customer service is a complete *joke*.
After the third delay, the schedule became a *joke*.

senses.gloss: A long process of personal change or growth.
examples: The book follows her *journey* from addiction to recovery.
Learning a language is a slow *journey*.
He spoke openly about his *journey* through grief.

senses.gloss: A thing or person that brings great happiness.
examples: Gardening is one of her few real *joys*.
That grandchild is a *joy*.
The book is about the small *joys* of everyday life.

senses.gloss: A person who decides the winner in a contest or competition.
examples: The *judges* gave her a perfect score.
She was a *judge* at the county fair's pie contest.
Three *judges* scored each routine.

senses.gloss: A person able to give a good opinion about the quality of something.
examples: He's a good *judge* of character.
I'm no *judge* of wine, but this one tastes fine.
She's a shrewd *judge* of talent.

senses.gloss: Electric power or fuel (informal).
examples: My phone is out of *juice*.
The storm knocked out the *juice* to half the block.
The old drill still has plenty of *juice*.

senses.gloss: The liquid that runs out of meat as it cooks.
examples: Let the roast rest so the *juices* settle.
Spoon the pan *juices* over the chicken.
The steak was still pink, with *juices* pooling on the plate.

senses.gloss: A confusing tangle of things that is hard to find your way through.
examples: The tax code is a *jungle*.
Her desk is a *jungle* of cords and paper.
Getting a permit means fighting through a *jungle* of forms.

senses.gloss: Someone who is younger than another person by a stated number of years.
examples: My brother is my *junior* by four years.
He married a woman twenty years his *junior*.
The new supervisor turned out to be her *junior* by a decade.
